The image shows a sugarcane leaf with a pale/whitish longitudinal stripe running along the midrib/center of the leaf. The surrounding leaf tissue appears predominantly green and healthy-looking. The stripe is elongated, following the leaf venation pattern.

**Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Leaf
- **Key features**: A single pale/silvery-white longitudinal stripe running along the central vein area of an otherwise green leaf
- **Pattern**: Linear, following the leaf axis — not spots, not mosaic mottling, not yellowing of the whole leaf

**Matching against classes:**

- **Brown_Spot**: Would show brown circular/oval spots — not matching
- **Grassy_Shoot**: Affects shoot morphology — not matching
- **Leaf_Scald**: Shows a water-soaked to pale stripe along leaf margins or veins, often with a distinct boundary — this is a strong candidate
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Affects young shoots with distortion/twisting — not matching
- **Sett_Rot**: Affects setts/roots — not matching
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Shows yellow/pale streaks mosaic pattern across the leaf — possible but mosaic usually more irregular
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Mosaic/mottled pattern with irregular yellow-green patches — not matching a single clean stripe
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Would show yellowing of midrib and leaf tissue — not matching (no yellow)
- **Yellow_Spot**: Would show yellow spots — not matching

The single pale/whitish elongated stripe along the leaf vein is most characteristic of **Leaf_Scald** (*Xanthomonas albilineans*), which causes white pencil-line stripes along the veins of sugarcane leaves. This matches very well with the pale longitudinal stripe visible in the image.
